title: Returned Premium Payments and the Monthly Bank-Draft Privilege — Term Life Insurance
content:
**Billing rules — Term Life Insurance.**

A payment returned unpaid by the bank reverses only the payment it names. Each returned payment is recorded once against the payment it reverses: a payment that already has a returned-payment entry is not returned a second time.

When a payment is returned, the installment it had paid becomes due again, the paid-to date moves back to that installment's due date, and the grace period for that installment is counted from its original due date, not from the date of the return.

**Monthly bank-draft (EFT) privilege.** Returned EFT drafts are counted over a rolling window of 12 calendar months ending on the date of the return being evaluated, both ends included: the count is the number of returned payments on the policy whose returned payment had been made by EFT, including the return being evaluated. When that count reaches the product's returned-EFT limit, the monthly EFT privilege ends: the premium mode is changed to quarterly direct billing effective with the next installment due, and monthly EFT may be elected again only after the product's re-enrollment wait in calendar months from the date of the return that ended the privilege.

Returned checks, card payments and one-time bank payments reverse the payment the same way but never count toward the EFT limit.

### Hypothetical count (limit of 2)

| Return date | Payment returned | Counted toward the EFT limit? | Count in the 12 months ending that date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 February | monthly EFT draft | yes | 1 |
| 5 June | check | no | 1 |
| 5 January of the next year | monthly EFT draft | yes | 2 — the limit is reached; quarterly direct billing from the next installment due |

Had the third return been dated 6 February of the next year, the 5 February return would fall outside the 12 months ending that date and the count would be 1.
